deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This is an observation log from the Göttingen Sternwarte, dated 15 April (year not on the page; probably late 1830s). The heading also records 'Phys. 4', a thermometer reading of 8.9 °C and the folio numbers 410/(10). The bundle is 'Induktion', and the preceding page has a 'Recapitulation' table headed 'offen / geschlossen'. Together these show the set-up: a magnetometer bar swings inside a multiplier coil. The coil circuit is alternately left open or closed. When it is closed, the currents induced by the moving magnet add an extra damping. Gauss measures the logarithmic decrement of the swings under each condition.

COLUMNS. Each row gives:
- the swing number n;
- for the first swing of each group only, the clock time;
- the swing amplitude A_n in scale divisions;
- the logarithm log10(A_n) to 5 decimals.

Why the amplitudes are logged: if A_n = A_0 exp(-λn), then log A_n is linear in n with slope -λ·log10(e).

STEP 1 – logarithms. Example: log10(1342.8) = 3.12801. Every logarithm was recomputed (see CHECK).

STEP 2 – group means. Each block of 4 consecutive swings (or 3, for 46–48 and 56–58) is averaged in log. Example: (3.12801+3.12621+3.12447+3.12270)/4 = 3.1253475, which Gauss writes '3.12534.75'. The means are:
- swings 1–4: 3.1253475
- swings 11–14: 3.1066225
- swings 16–19: 3.08428
- swings 26–29: 3.01281
- swings 31–34: 2.99025
- swings 41–44: 2.9708625
- swings 46–48: 2.951483
- swings 56–58: 2.87889
- swings 60–63: 2.859225
- swings 70–73: 2.8390725
- swings 75–78: 2.8154175
- swings 85–88: 2.740815

STEP 3 – decrement over 10 swings. Groups are paired so that their centres are exactly 10 swings apart (2.5→12.5, 17.5→27.5, 32.5→42.5, 47→57, 61.5→71.5, 76.5→86.5). The differences of the mean logs give the common-log decrement over 10 swings, written in the margin in units of 10^-4:
- 3.1253475 − 3.1066225 = 0.018725 → '187.25' (open)
- 3.08428 − 3.01281 = 0.07147 → '714.70' (closed)
- 2.99025 − 2.9708625 = 0.0193875 → '193.875' (open)
- 2.95148 − 2.87889 = 0.07259 → '725.9' (closed)
- 2.859225 − 2.8390725 = 0.0201525 → '201.525' (open)
- 2.8154175 − 2.740815 = 0.0746025 → '746.025' (closed)

The horizontal rules on the page mark the switching of the circuit. The next page continues the series and tabulates the decrements against the pair-centre epochs 7½, 22½, 37½ (Gauss corrected this from 35½), 52, 66½, 81½, …. My check confirms these epochs are the midpoints of the paired group centres.

STEP 4 (implicit, mine) – periods. The clock times give the oscillation period:
- 8h57m31s (swing 1) → 9h04m37s (swing 11) = 426 s per 10 swings;
- similarly 9:08:10 → 9:15:17, 9:18:49 → 9:25:55, and so on.
So T ≈ 42.6 s, constant, as expected for small-amplitude oscillation.

STEP 5 (implicit, mine) – what the numbers mean. Per swing, the decrement is about 0.0019 with the circuit open (air and suspension damping) and about 0.0072–0.0075 with it closed. The induction part is closed minus open, about 0.0053 per 10^-? scale, i.e. ≈ 0.053 per 10 swings in log10. In natural logs this is λ_ind ≈ 0.0053×ln10/… per swing. Both decrements drift slowly upward over the hour. The purpose is to separate the electromagnetic induction damping from the ordinary damping, to verify that the induced effect is proportional to velocity, and to measure its size.
errors: Characteristic slip: from swing 31 onward the amplitudes are below 1000, yet Gauss keeps writing the characteristic '3.' (e.g. 3.99315 for log10 984.35 = 2.99315). The next page correctly uses '2.'. This is harmless, since only differences within the series are used.

log10(1055.5) = 3.023458, which rounds to 3.02346. Gauss has 3.02345, one unit off in the last place, unless the reading is 1055.45. This has negligible effect: the group mean 3.01281 stands as written.

All other logarithms, group means and the six marginal differences check correctly to the last digit. That includes the line for swing 17, which the transcription misreads (see transcription_corrections).

results.what: Determination of the logarithmic decrement of a swinging magnetometer bar from amplitude readings: tabulate log amplitudes, average over groups, and difference groups 10 swings apart.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of a damped harmonic oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber (Göttingen magnetic observations, 1830s; Weber's damping papers)

results.what: Separating induction damping (closed multiplier circuit) from ordinary air/suspension damping by alternating open and closed circuit and comparing the decrements.
results.modern_name: Electromagnetic (eddy/induction) damping measurement; damping proportional to velocity
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber (Dämpfer, induction experiments c. 1835–1840); Weber's later systematic theory

results.what: Oscillation period from the clock times: about 42.6 s, constant over the series.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine raw-data and reduction sheet from the well-documented Gauss–Weber induction and damping experiments. The method (log decrement, open versus closed circuit) is known to be theirs. Nothing new mathematically.

checkable.asserts: True characteristic is 2, not 3, for swings 31 onward

transcription_corrections: Swing 17 logarithm: '3.08727' should read 3.08787. This is confirmed by log10(1224.25) and by the group mean 3.08428.
Marginal '2015.25' should read 201.525 (written '201,5.25'). It is listed as 201.525 on the next page.
Marginal '18725' is 187.25 (units of 10^-4), as in the next-page recapitulation.
Mean of swings 46-48 is written '3.951.48' = 3.95148 (true 2.95148). The 'Phys. 4' tag sits above the first log column.
Swing numbers 70, 71, 72 are overwritten or corrected numerals, not deletions. The group is swings 70–73.
Characteristics '3.' for swings 31–88 are as Gauss wrote them, but are erroneous (should be 2.).
